texts.preamble: Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Madhu Jain Principal District & Sessions Judge: South District, Saket Courts, New Delhi Crl. Appeal No.357/2023 Cnr No.-DLST01-012753-2023 Prem Prakash S/O Sh. Phool Singh R/O K-2Nd 355, 3Rd Floor, Sangam Vihar New Delhi - 110080. .....Appellant / Husband Versus Urmila W/O Sh. Prem Prakash R/O A-56, 1St Floor, Jj Colony, Tigri, Phase - I, New Delhi - 110062. .....Respondent /Wife Date of Institution : 21.12.2023 Arguments Concluded on : 16.04.2025 Date of Judgment : 16.04.2025 Judgment
texts.facts: Besides this, learned MM also awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- as compensation to the respondent to be paid by the appellant. 2. The facts in brief as per the record are that the appellant got married to the respondent on 28.11.2005. It has been stated that parents of the complainant/respondent spent sufficient amount at the time of marriage and gave dowry articles to the appellant and his family members as per their demands. However, she was subjected to mental and physical torture, beatings and other cruelties Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/ 1 time and again by the appellant and his family members for bringing less dowry. The respondent / complainant has narrated various incidents of abuses, humiliation and beatings by the appellant and his family members. The matter was even reported to Police also on 03.06.2008 and appellant and his brother were also sent to jail by learned SEM. Also, before CAW Cell Amar Colony, the appellant and his brother refused to take back the CA No.357/2023 madhu by madhu jain Date: jain 2025.04.17 Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila 15:47:03 +0530 respondent to matrimonial home even after the order of learned SEM. Thereafter, only with the intervention of police, the appellant took the respondent to matrimonial home. But, even after several dates of hearing before CAW Cell, appellant continued to harass, torture and give beatings to the respondent and thrown her out of matrimonial house and also, flatly refused to take her back. With the help of CAW officials, the respondent was again sent back to her matrimonial house on 04.08.2008. Thereafter, the respondent was sent back to her parental house in wearing clothes only on the occasions of Rakhi and Bhai Dooj and she was not given any jewellery. In order to save her marriage, the respondent/complainant continued to reside in the matrimonial home with the hope that the appellant would mend his behavior. Despite facing continuous harassment, humiliation, and ill-treatment, she chose to bear all the atrocities for the sake of preserving the marital relationship. However, the appellant failed to change his conduct, which ultimately compelled her to take legal recourse and she filed a complaint against appellant with PS Neb Sarai on 17.04.2009. On 20.04.2009, when the appellant and his brother came to know about that complaint, they started throwing household articles and also gave beatings to complainant/respondent. Consequently, respondent called the police and appellant and madhu by madhu jain Date: jain 2025.04.17 15:47:08 +0530 his brother were taken to police station from where they ran away and reached to their house and put two big locks on the same. Thereafter, the appellant and his brother did not return. Having no other option, respondent started living with his sister Kavita, who was also residing in another portion of matrimonial house being the wife of brother of appellant. Since all the clothes and articles of the respondent were lying in locked house, she made requests to appellant and his family members to let her stay in matrimonial house which they refused. Feeling aggrieved with the atrocities committed upon her by the appellant and his family members by refusing shelter, food, clothing and other day to day requirements, the respondent filed a petition under Section 12 of DV Act before the learned Trial court seeking various reliefs. 3. The appellant herein duly contested the petition and filed reply wherein he denied all the allegations made against him by the respondent / complainant. It has been stated that appellant had been living separately since April 2009 and he filed a petition under Section 9 of HMA for restitution of conjugal rights and got issued a legal notice which was duly served upon the respondent. It has also been stated that the respondent is residing in the house which is in the name of mother of appellant and she has no right to force his parents to leave that house. Rather, the Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/ 2 respondent is enjoying the madhu by madhu jain CA No.357/2023 jain Date: 2025.04.17 15:47:13 +0530 whole of the property which belongs to the mother of appellant and thus, she is not entitled to any relief instead she is liable to reside with the appellant. It has been stated that it is the respondent who has deserted the appellant willfully and thus, she is not entitled to any maintenance or compensation from the appellant. 4. Both the parties filed their income and expenditure affidavits before the learned trial court and thereafter, led their respective evidences. Aggrieved of the same, the appellant / husband has preferred the present appeal.
texts.arguments: 5. The appellant has challenged the impugned order on the grounds that learned trial court while disposing the complaint under Section 12 of DV Act has not at all considered the cross examination of the complainant's witnesses who have contradicted each other and failed to make out a case of domestic violence ; that learned trial court has failed to consider the submissions made by the appellant that it was the CA No.357/2023 madhu by madhu jain Date: jain 2025.04.17 Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila 15:47:18 +0530 respondent who had committed cruelties upon the appellant and his family members ; that learned trial court has failed to appreciate that respondent preferred an appeal before the Sessions court against the order of learned Predecessor of trial court whereby the court was pleased to vacate the stay order granted vide order dated 29.05.2009 but the respondent failed to comply with the order ; that learned trial court has failed to consider that mother-in-law and father-in-law of respondent have been constrained to file a suit for possession of the house owned by them which is pending adjudication before learned ADJ as the respondent is living in the house belonging to mother of the appellant and respondent instead of vacating the house filed appeals before Hon'ble High Court which are still pending disposal ; that learned trial court has failed to consider that respondent alongwith her sister is occupying the other house owned by father of the appellant and whole family is living in a rented accommodation since 2009 ; that learned trial court has failed to consider that respondent and her sister are filing bogus cases against the appellant and his family in order to harass them ; that learned trial court has failed to take into account that respondent is having sufficient means to sustain herself and the minor son as she is earning good income from stitching work which she has duly admitted in her reply and evidence affidavit hence, madhu by madhu jain Date: jain 2025.04.17 15:47:23 +0530 she is not entitled to any maintenance ; that learned trial court has failed to consider that minor son of the parties is studying in Atulasha Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/ 3 School under EWS scheme whereby he has been provided all the facilities free of cost ; that learned trial court has failed to consider that respondent and her sister have filed false cases against the appellant and old aged parents which have culminated into registration of FIRs bearing No.45/2010 and 46/2010 PS Neb Sarai under Sections 406/498A/34 IPC ; that learned trial court while passing the impugned judgment has failed to consider the cross examination conducted on the witnesses of the respondent where they have not at all corroborated the version given by respondent and thus, she has not been able to prove any domestic violence having been committed upon her by the appellant ; that learned trial court has failed to consider that appellant has been regularly paying the amount of maintenance so fixed by the court. 6. The appeal is duly contested by the respondent by filing reply wherein it has been stated that the present appeal has been filed by the appellant only to harass the respondent and her minor son and to deprive them of their valuable rights to get maintenance and residence. Hence, the same is liable to be dismissed. 7. Learned counsel for the appellant has vehemently argued that learned trial court has granted maintenance at an exorbitant CA No.357/2023 madhu Digitally signed by madhu jain Date: 2025.04.17 jain 15:47:27 +0530 rate of Rs.5,000/- from the date of filing of complaint. It has been stated that vide order dated 20.08.2009 interim maintenance of Rs.2,000/- per month was granted by learned trial court for both respondent and minor son and since, the respondent was aware of the condition of the appellant she did not challenge the same by filing any appeal against that order. From the same, it is apparent that respondent is earning sufficiently hence, she does not require any maintenance. Learned counsel further argued that learned trial court erred in passing the impugned judgment as it has failed to take into account that respondent had failed to comply with the vacating order dated 29.05.2009, and instead, continued to unlawfully occupy the house owned by the appellant's mother and a separate possession suit filed by the appellant's parents in this regard is pending adjudication. He further pointed out that the respondent and her sister are occupying another property owned by the appellant's father, forcing the appellant's family to live in rented accommodation since 2009. It has been argued that respondent and her sister have filed multiple false and frivolous complaints against the appellant and his family members including FIRs No.45/2010 and 46/2010 under Sections 406/498A/34 IPC. It has been argued that the minor child of the parties is receiving education under the EWS scheme free of cost and now he has madhu by madhu jain Date: jain 2025.04.17 15:47:32 +0530 attained majority. Learned counsel also argued that respondent is living a comfortable life and is earning sufficiently which is evident from the fact that she is filing multiple litigation against the appellant and his family members and spending huge amount on legal proceedings whereas, the appellant is residing in rental accommodation and suffering from various health problems. It has been argued that the impugned judgment passed by the learned trial court is erroneous and based on a misapprehension of the appellant's financial position and without considering the fact that there is no supporting evidence to the averments Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/ 4 made by the respondent with respect to incidents of domestic violence. Moreover, the appellant has been regularly complying with the maintenance orders passed by the court. Hence, it is submitted that the respondent is not entitled to the relief granted, and the impugned judgment deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Besides addressing oral arguments, written arguments have also been filed on behalf of the appellant. 8. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent argued that learned trial court has rightly passed the impugned judgment giving detailed observations and after considering the entire material placed on record as well as the evidence led by both the parties and thus, there is no reason to interfere in the findings of the learned trial court. Further, learned trial madhu by madhu jain CA No.357/2023 jain Date: 2025.04.17 15:47:36 Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila +0530 court has also duly considered the facts of the case and has very fairly assessed the income of the appellant on minimum wage rate and rightly awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month for the respondent and minor child. Learned counsel has argued that all the contentions raised before this court by the appellant have already been dealt in detail by the learned trial court and thus, there is no illegality or impropriety in the impugned judgment. Therefore, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. During the course of arguments, respondent has stated that child has just completed 12th class. It has also come on record that the parties are living separately since April 2009. 11. The grievances of the appellant are that the order granting Rs.5,000/- monthly maintenance from the date of the complaint is excessive in view of the financial condition of the appellant. It has been contended that the appellant is suffering from health issues and is already complying with maintenance orders and thus, the respondent is not liable to any maintenance. These laws recognize that domestic Prem Prakash vs Urmila on 16 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48520552/ 5 violence is not limited to physical harm but also includes emotional, verbal, sexual, and economic abuse. 17. Despite the appellant's vague and questionable claims, learned trial court did not rely solely on his affidavit but instead took a fair and objective approach and assessed his CA No.357/2023 madhu by Prem Prakash Vs. Urmila jain Date: 2025.04.17 income by referring to an official government order that specifies the minimum wages for unskilled laborers in Delhi i.e. Rs.17,494/- per month.
